description: Your agent invents things because it has no memory, and can't touch your database because it has no arms. rsc is the meta-harness that gives it both, plus the trade to know the job and the reflexes to not break your repo. For Claude Code, Codex and 15 more.

curation.summary: rsc-harness is a CLI tool and npm package that generates and installs project-specific 'harnesses' for AI coding assistants, giving agents memory, skills, and tool access across 18+ assistant targets including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Cline. It uses a plan-first approach where it reads project evidence, asks about goals, and presents an installable plan for user approval before making changes.
curation.whyNotable: It addresses a real pain point in the AI coding assistant ecosystem: the fragmentation of configuration across different tools and the lack of project-level memory and context. The meta-harness concept—using a tool to configure and standardize other AI tools—is genuinely novel and fills a gap between open standards (Agent Skills, MCP, AGENTS.md) and practical project setup.
strengths: Novel meta-harness concept that configures AI assistants rather than being one itself
Broad support for 18+ assistant targets with 274 skills available
Plan-first workflow ensures user consent before modifying project files
Excellent documentation with clear visual guides, tables, and onboarding flow
Built on open standards (Agent Skills, MCP, AGENTS.md) ensuring interoperability
Very active development with 100 releases and CI/tests in place
limitations: Very new project (created May 2026) with limited track record and no Docker support
No examples directory, which could make it harder to understand advanced use cases
JavaScript-only, limiting accessibility for non-JS developers
Faces compatibility risk from the rapidly evolving AI assistant ecosystem it depends on
The crowded AI dev tools space makes differentiation challenging long-term
useCases: Standardizing AI assistant configuration across a development team or multiple projects
Onboarding a new developer to a project by giving their AI assistant full project context
Migrating between AI coding assistants while preserving project knowledge and skills
Setting up memory and tool access for AI agents to interact with databases and internal APIs
curation.targetAudience: Developers and engineering teams who use multiple AI coding assistants and want consistent, well-configured agent setups with project-specific knowledge and skills.
curation.oneLiner: A meta-harness CLI that generates and installs project-specific configurations, skills, and memory for 18+ AI coding assistants with a plan-first, user-approved workflow.

name: mxc
description: Policy-driven, layered isolation and containment

curation.summary: MXC (Microsoft eXecution Container) is a cross-platform sandboxed code execution system that provides policy-driven isolation for running untrusted code across Windows, Linux, and macOS. It offers a unified containment model with multiple backends ranging from OS-native process sandboxes to full VMs, exposed through Rust, .NET, and Node SDKs.
curation.whyNotable: Backed by Microsoft, MXC addresses a critical security need for AI applications—safely executing LLM-generated code, plugins, and tools. Its unified abstraction across diverse containment backends (Bubblewrap, Seatbelt, Windows Sandbox, MicroVM, etc.) with a typed policy model is a sophisticated approach to a hard problem.
strengths: Unified containment model across multiple backends (OS-native sandboxes, VMs, containers) with a consistent policy-driven API
True cross-platform support (Windows, Linux, macOS) with platform-appropriate backend selection
Well-designed typed SDKs in Rust, .NET, and Node with versioned configuration
Strong Microsoft engineering backing with CI, tests, and regular releases
limitations: Relatively new project (created Feb 2026) with 117 open issues and several experimental backends
No Docker support or examples directory, limiting quick evaluation
Not a pure AI/ML project—fits outside the 9-category AI taxonomy as general security infrastructure
useCases: Safely executing untrusted LLM-generated code or model output
Isolating third-party plugins and tools in AI agent applications
Multi-tenant code execution platforms and secure CI/CD pipelines
Enterprise environments requiring policy-driven application containment
curation.targetAudience: Developers and platform engineers building applications that need to execute untrusted code, particularly those working on AI agents, LLM applications, or multi-tenant execution environments.
curation.oneLiner: Microsoft's unified, policy-driven sandboxing SDK for safely running untrusted code across Windows, Linux, and macOS with multiple containment backends.
